data.body_html:
Thinking about a Marbella boat rental in January? You might be surprised – winter on the Costa del Sol can offer crisp, clear days with calm seas, and you'll have the coastline almost to yourself. This guide covers January weather, sea conditions, what to wear, and which of our boats are best for a winter charter. All departures are from Puerto Banús.

January Weather in Marbella: The Numbers

January is Marbella's coolest month, but 'cool' is relative. Average daily highs reach 17°C, and overnight lows drop to around 8°C. You can expect about 5-6 hours of sunshine per day – enough for a pleasant cruise. Rainfall averages 70mm, making it the wettest month, but showers are usually short and pass quickly.

  • Average high: 17°C
  • Average low: 8°C
  • Sunshine: 5-6 hours/day
  • Rainfall: 70mm (wettest month)
  • Sea temperature: 15°C

Sea Conditions: Calm Days and Levante Winds

The Mediterranean around Marbella is calm about 60% of the time in January. However, the Levante wind (from the east) can bring choppy seas and a few knots of wind. Our skippers check forecasts daily and will recommend the best time to sail. On calm days, you can cruise along the coast to Cabopino or even Estepona.

What to Wear for a Winter Boat Trip

Layering is key. Start with a thermal base, add a fleece, and top with a waterproof windbreaker. A beanie and gloves are wise. Non-slip shoes are essential. Don't forget sunscreen – the sun can still be strong. Our boats have heated saloons, so you can warm up between sightings.

Our Boats for January Charters

All boats in our fleet are available year-round, weather permitting. For winter, enclosed flybridge models offer the most comfort. The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) has a spacious saloon with heating. The Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) is a superyacht experience. If you want speed and style, the Pershing 46 (14m, 10 pax) is a great choice.

What's Included in Every Charter

Every rental includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden extras. You just show up and enjoy.

January Highlights: What to See

Even in January, the coastline is stunning. Cruise past the Golden Mile, see La Concha mountain dusted with snow, and anchor near Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés. You might spot dolphins – sightings are common in winter. For a longer trip, head to Estepona or Sotogrande.

Book Your January Charter

Ready to experience Marbella from the sea in January? Browse our full fleet and send us a WhatsApp for availability. For the best value, book a Tier A boat like the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39. If you want a larger vessel, the Mangusta 80 includes a free jet ski. Check our blog for more seasonal guides.
